diagnosis: Acute on chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
hospital_course: You came in with leg swelling, weight gain, and shortness of breath when lying flat. You received IV water pills and lost about 6 pounds of fluid. Your breathing is now comfortable and your discharge weight is 168 pounds.

medications.name: Furosemide
medications.note: This is a water pill. Take it in the morning so you are not up at night.

medications.name: Lisinopril
medications.note: Do not use potassium salt substitutes.

medications.name: Metoprolol succinate
medications.note: Do not crush or chew it. Do not stop it suddenly.

diet: Limit sodium to less than 2,000 mg per day. Avoid canned soups, deli meats, and fast food.
Limit fluids to 64 ounces (about 2 liters) per day, including soup, ice, and coffee.
activity: Walk 10 to 15 minutes twice a day and rest when tired. Raise your legs when sitting.
No lifting over 10 pounds for 2 weeks.
care: Weigh yourself every morning after you urinate, before you eat, in the same clothes, and write it down.
monitoring: Call us if you gain more than 3 pounds in 1 day or 5 pounds in 1 week.
Check your blood pressure and pulse every morning for 7 days.

follow_up.who: Dr. Maria Castillo, Heart Failure Clinic
follow_up.purpose: a post-hospital visit, weight check, and blood tests

warning_signs: severe trouble breathing, especially when lying down
a very fast or irregular heartbeat
call_clinic: weight gain of more than 3 pounds in 1 day or 5 pounds in 1 week
more swelling in your legs or belly
